title: Ranges and references
summary: Select ranges that span several columns, and use cell names inside formulas so results update by themselves.
intro:
A range can span several columns and rows at once, such as `B2:D5`. Functions use ranges to refer to a whole group of values in one go.

When you type a cell name inside a formula, it is a reference to that cell. The power of references is that the result updates by itself whenever the values change, without retyping anything.

faq.q: How many cells are in the range `B2:D5`?
faq.a: Three columns (B, C and D) by four rows (2 to 5), so 12 cells.

faq.q: Why type `=B2` instead of the number itself?
faq.a: A reference follows the cell: if its value changes, the result changes automatically. A typed number stays fixed.

select-a-block.prompt: These are the study hours of four students. A range can span several columns and rows. Select Layla's and Omar's hours for the three days: the range `B2:D3`.
select-a-block.hint: Start at `B2` and drag to `D3`, or use Shift with the arrow keys.

select-all-numbers.prompt: Select all the hours in the table. The first cell of this range is `B2` and the last is `D5`.

first-reference.prompt: When you type a cell name inside a formula, it is a reference to that cell. In `F2`, type the formula `=B2` to show Layla's hours on Sunday.
first-reference.hint: Start with `=`, then type `B2`. Don't type the number 2 yourself.
first-reference.explain: If the value in `B2` changes, the result in `F2` changes automatically.

add-with-references.prompt: In `E2`, type a formula that adds Layla's hours for the three days: `=B2+C2+D2`.

same-for-omar.prompt: In `E3`, type a formula the same way to add Omar's hours.

cells-in-a-range.prompt: How many cells are in the range `B2:C4`?
cells-in-a-range.hint: Two columns (B and C) by three rows (2, 3 and 4).
